instructions: Click on the SUBMIT button for the object you wish to image.
Click on System Status or View Observatory to view the status of your plan execution in real-time.
Once the exposure has finished, the image will be ready for download in approximately 5 minutes.
notes: Astronomical objects listed below are at least 45 degrees above the horizon.
If you are a beginner, start with the brightest targets first and work your way to the least bright.
Previews are indicative of a multiple long exposures images aligned, stacked with noise rejection and post image processing applied.

workflow: Confirm coordinates and visibility with the iTelescope Planning Tool or Telescopius.
Check framing in Telescopius with the correct telescope selected.
Fill out the Deep Sky Imaging and Planning form; RA/DEC in most formats, suggested HH:MM:SS and DD:MM:SS (e.g. RA 05:23:25 DEC -10:12:56).
Use the shortest sub-exposures that give good signal to noise.
Click Acquire Images Now, or Create Plan For Later to schedule via the Reservation system.
Watch via System Status or View Desktop (/ac/MenuItems/remote.asp).
Image ready about 5 minutes after the exposure finishes.
tips: Shorter subs reduce bad frames from conditions and cosmic rays.
Stack many shorter subs, e.g. 120 s x 10 = 1200 s master, rather than one 1200 s frame.
Ideal sub length: sky shot noise just exceeds camera dark current noise.
Brighter object means shorter subs; darker filter means longer subs; narrowband (Ha, SII, OIII) needs longer than wideband.
Match sub length to an existing dark frame (Darks 600 s Bin1).
Dither each sub to reduce noise.
Use #REPEAT n with 1 exposure per filter instead of Qty n per filter, so a plan cut short still has every filter.
notes: Telescope refocuses periodically and on temperature change; #FORCESTARTUP + #NOADAPTIVE disables this.
Max imaging time 600 s, min elevation 23 deg, suggested 45 deg or more.
